Tomato Healthy.name: Tomato Healthy
Tomato Healthy.symptoms: Even green foliage with no visible lesions.
Tomato Healthy.prevention: Monitor regularly for changes in color, texture, or leaf shape.

Tomato Early Blight.name: Tomato Early Blight
Tomato Early Blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings on lower leaves.
Tomato Early Blight.cause: Fungal infection caused by Alternaria solani.
Tomato Early Blight.treatment: Remove affected leaves, improve air circulation, and follow appropriate fungicide recommendations.
Tomato Early Blight.prevention: Maintain leaf spacing, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, and remove bottom leaves.

Tomato Late Blight.name: Tomato Late Blight
Tomato Late Blight.symptoms: Dark, water-soaked lesions that spread quickly across leaves.
Tomato Late Blight.cause: Phytophthora infestans, favored by cool and humid conditions.
Tomato Late Blight.treatment: Remove infected material and follow appropriate fungicide recommendations.
Tomato Late Blight.prevention: Water at the soil line, provide airflow, and avoid working with wet foliage.

Potato Healthy.name: Potato Healthy
Potato Healthy.symptoms: Healthy green foliage without visible spots or lesions.
Potato Healthy.treatment: Continue normal crop care and monitor plant growth.
Potato Healthy.prevention: Use clean planting material and inspect foliage regularly.

Potato Early Blight.name: Potato Early Blight
Potato Early Blight.symptoms: Small brown lesions with target-like rings on older leaves.
Potato Early Blight.treatment: Remove severely affected leaves and follow local fungicide guidance.
Potato Early Blight.prevention: Rotate crops, reduce leaf wetness, and remove crop debris.

Potato Late Blight.name: Potato Late Blight
Potato Late Blight.symptoms: Irregular dark lesions with possible pale margins.
Potato Late Blight.treatment: Remove infected plants promptly and follow professional crop protection guidance.
Potato Late Blight.prevention: Provide airflow and avoid overhead irrigation.

Pepper Healthy.name: Pepper Healthy
Pepper Healthy.symptoms: Plant appears healthy with even green foliage and no visible lesions.
Pepper Healthy.treatment: Continue regular watering, feeding, and routine maintenance.
Pepper Healthy.prevention: Monitor regularly for changes in color, texture, or leaf shape.

Pepper Bacterial Spot.name: Pepper Bacterial Spot
Pepper Bacterial Spot.symptoms: Small dark spots that may develop pale centers on leaves.
Pepper Bacterial Spot.cause: Bacterial infection favored by warm, wet conditions.
Pepper Bacterial Spot.treatment: Remove affected material, keep foliage dry, and follow local agricultural guidance.
Pepper Bacterial Spot.prevention: Use clean seed, improve airflow, and avoid handling wet plants.
